newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka fines two firms for exchange violations.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka fines two firms for exchange violations.

text.p: Sri Lanka has fined two companies for violating exchange control regulations during the sale of a state-owned plantation firm in 1995, a senior government official said on Tuesday.
Lankem Ceylon Ltd and Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka Ltd had each been fined in the region of 100 million rupees ($1.7 million) each, said the official, who declined to be identified.
"Lankem has been fined for paying money to a non-national without prior permission from the Exchange Controller," he said.
The Exchange Control Act requires those buying and selling assets to foreigners to get prior permission.
On Monday, Lankem said in a letter to the Colombo Stock Exchange it had been fined 115.5 million rupees.
"The company totally denies any contravention...and will be appealing immediately against the imposition of such penalty," it said.
A person found guilty of violating provisions of the Exchange Control Act can appeal to the Minister of Finance.
Merchant Bank, an investment bank, was fined for arranging the transaction, which the official said was "tantamount to a violation of the regulation".
The government official said the violations took place when Kotagala Plantations Ltd was privatised in 1995.

A stake was bought by a unit of Sri Lankan tea firm George Steuarts Ltd, which subsequently sold out to a Malaysian national. Lankem Ceylon Ltd bought control of Kotagala plantations from the Malaysian.
Both George Steuarts and the Malaysian had also been fined by the Exchange controller, the official said.
